subject: Scheduling demo during DST transition — timezone options
messages:
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@blueriverpayments.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 20:03:00 +0100
Subject: Quick: scheduling a demo next week

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the intro. We’re excited to see Redwood in action — mainly focused on latency/cost tradeoffs for heavy-transaction workloads. Can we lock a 45min demo with the engineering and payments teams next week? A few windows that work for us (Berlin time):

- Tue, Mar 10 — 10:00–10:45 CET
- Wed, Mar 11 — 14:00–14:45 CET

We have two folks in APAC (Singapore) who can join early if necessary, and two folks on the East Coast US who will be joining remotely.

Prefer Tue morning CET but happy to move if it’s a pain on your side.

Best,
Jamie
Jamie Lee
Head of Integrations, BlueRiver Payments
attachment: agenda-draft.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@blueriverpayments.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick: scheduling a demo next week

Hi Jamie — thanks, excited to run this. Quick note on timing: the US switches to daylight saving time on Sun, Mar 8 (clocks move forward one hour). Europe (CET) doesn’t switch until later in March. That means a time that looks normal in CET on Mar 10 maps to different local hours for our US folks than it would before Mar 8.

To avoid confusion for your East Coast and West Coast attendees, here are a couple of options (all dates are for the proposed Tue, Mar 10):

Option A — keep it at your requested slot:
- 10:00 CET (Berlin) on Tue Mar 10 → 05:00 EDT (New York), 02:00 PDT (San Francisco), 17:00 SGT (Singapore)

Option B — shift to a more US-friendly overlap (better for East Coast):
- 13:00 CET → 08:00 EDT, 05:00 PDT, 20:00 SGT

Option C — a later CET time that’s OK for APAC (if APAC attendance is critical):
- 16:00 CET → 11:00 EDT, 08:00 PDT, 23:00 SGT

If you’d like, I can propose a calendar time that resolves the DST delta and include conversion notes for each region. I’ve attached a quick timezone comparison chart for Mar 9–11 that highlights the US/EU offset after Mar 8.

Which option do you prefer? Vanessa and Sergio — flag if any of these conflict with our demo engineers’ schedules; we should try to have a recording option if the US early hour is unavoidable.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@blueriverpayments.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 15:35:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Quick: scheduling a demo next week

Alex — thanks for the clear breakdown. For this account I’d prefer Option B (13:00 CET) so their East Coast folks have a normal morning slot and we don’t force anyone into a 05:00 start. Sergio, can you confirm you can cover the runtime/quantization section at 08:00 EDT on Tue Mar 10? If not, we’ll either slide to 16:00 CET or record the runtime deep-dive and run it as a follow-up session.

Also: when you send the calendar invite, please include a short note about the DST shift so attendees don’t assume an earlier US local time.

Vanessa Ortiz
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Vanessa / Sergio — thanks for the clarification and options. Let’s go with Option B: Tue Mar 10 at 13:00 CET (that should be 08:00 EDT for our New York folks). Eli and I will block time and we’ll forward the invite to our APAC colleagues (they can join late if needed).

Looking forward to it — agenda looks good.

Best,
Jamie
